QF.id: XXVA Regulatory Compliance for Non-Core Research Personnel_21

question.text: A sales person at a research entity selectively shares upcoming research recommendations with a preferred client before publication. This conduct primarily violates which requirement?

answer.text: The duty to build strong client relationships
The rule that a research report cannot be made available selectively to a particular client before other entitled clients, and that confidentiality must be maintained until the report is public
Only an internal sales policy, not any regulatory requirement
A requirement that applies only if the preferred client trades on the information

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook requires that a research report must not be made selectively available to a particular client in advance of other entitled clients, and that confidentiality of the report must be maintained until it is made public. Selective pre-publication sharing directly contravenes both rules. The Trap: Whether or not the preferred client traded is not what determines the breach — the act of selective advance distribution is itself the violation. It is not merely an internal sales matter, nor is it consistent with proper client servicing. Note: The explanation relies on the source-supported confidentiality and fair-distribution rules; no claims about personal regulatory consequences are added.
